role: The original named in rendition_of stays the source and keeps its record; this rendition is what the guide shows. Make any new size, crop or print file from the original (or from the Commons original at original_url), never from this rendition.
decision: DR-238, Dustin, November 12, 2026: "I approve the smaller photographs" (board 1, question 1c; D3-193). The guide shows chapter 01's photographs at 600 px wide at most, so 1,200 px covers a 2x screen.

method.steps: Image.open(original); resize((1200, round(height * 1200 / width)), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS); save(JPEG, quality=85, optimize=True, progressive=True, icc_profile=the original's)
method.color_profile: none: the original carries no ICC profile, so none is added (read as sRGB)
method.rights_metadata: none to keep: the original carries no EXIF, XMP, IPTC or comment segment (Wikimedia's standard-width rendition strips them); the rights are in this record
method.same_as: The engineer's board 1 measure (weight_options.py, photo_saving), which gave 223,719 bytes for this photograph

download_note: Downloaded on November 6, 2026 as Wikimedia's standard-width rendition of the original, through the imageinfo API. The original URL returned HTTP 429 with Retry-After 600 three times, and Wikimedia's error page directs rate-limited clients to its standard thumbnail sizes. Replace with the original from original_url before print, and check it against original_sha1.

source_description: From October 30-31, 2005, Rosa Parks lay in honor in the Capitol Rotunda. Parks was the first woman to lay in honor in the Capitol Rotunda and the second African-American. ... Authority for use of the Rotunda granted by Senate Concurrent Resolution 61, 109th Congress, 1st Session, agreed to October 29, 2005.
caption: Members of the public file past the casket of Rosa Parks, the civil rights pioneer, as she lies in honor in the Rotunda of the U.S. Capitol, Washington, D.C., October 2005. Photograph: Architect of the Capitol.
why_it_fits: A documentary photograph in which the Capitol Rotunda (its pilasters, historical paintings and statues) appears as the place where a named public event happened. The subject is the public filing past the casket; no partisan figure is the subject.
notes: The Architect of the Capitol mark sits at the lower right; crop it. Uniformed U.S. Capitol Police officers stand in the line of mourners.
